sections.h2: Under one in ten new cars had emergency-braking driver aids in 2025

chart.title: Share of new cars with driver-assistance systems rose from 6.43% to 8.41%
chart.sub: Share of passenger vehicles sold with advanced driver-assistance systems, %.
chart.source: Counterpoint Research, as reported in the draft coverage.

sections.means: Most equipped cars are utility vehicles, and the cheapest car with full driver assistance is the top variant of the Maruti Baleno.
sections.todo: Carmakers should add emergency braking to entry-level variants now, rather than waiting for the 2030 and 2032 dates.

sections.h2: Europe made AEB compulsory in 2024; India's full mandate lands in 2032

events: EU: new car types must have AEB
EU: all new cars must have AEB
US: FMVSS 127 applies to all light vehicles
India: every new car model must have AEB
India: every car built must have AEB

sections.means: The draft gives carmakers four years to redesign new models and six to change models already in production.
sections.todo: Regulators should bring the India dates forward, or tie them to the Bharat NCAP 2.0 protocol expected from October 2027.

sections.h2: Crashes where a vehicle is hit from behind caused about a fifth of road deaths in 2023

chart.title: Hit-from-behind crashes caused 34,578 deaths in 2023, out of 172,890 road deaths
chart.source: India road accident data for 2023, as cited in the draft coverage.

sections.means: AEB in cars addresses only part of this total, the crashes where a car is the one doing the hitting and those involving pedestrians.
sections.todo: The ministry should publish a breakdown of rear-end deaths by vehicle role, so the rule can be judged against it.
